title: Gauss-Bonnet Theorem: Curvature to Euler Characteristic

problemStatement.formal: theorem discrete_gauss_bonnet (S : PolyhedralSurface) : S.totalDeficiency = 2 * π * S.chi
problemStatement.plain: The discrete Gauss-Bonnet theorem: the sum of angular deficiencies over all vertices of a polyhedral surface equals 2π times its Euler characteristic.
whyMatters: Connects local curvature to global topology
Bridges combinatorial Euler formula with differential geometry

proven: All 5 Platonic solids verified with per-vertex deficiency
Schlafli constraint gives exactly 5 regular polyhedra
knownResults.goal: Prove discrete Gauss-Bonnet theorem connecting angular deficiency to Euler characteristic

insights: Algebraic double-counting avoids differential geometry entirely
Total face angles = (2E-2F)π via handshaking for faces
exact_mod_cast handles ℕ→ℤ→ℝ casting chains better than push_cast+linarith

approaches.name: algebraic-double-counting
approaches.description: Use handshaking lemma for faces: Σp_F = 2E. Total face angles = (2E-2F)π. Then Σδ(v) = 2πV - (2E-2F)π = 2π(V-E+F) = 2πχ.
